items.stem: Detecting hidden microscopic structural cracks deep inside thick metallic blocks. Which of these practical applications fundamentally rely on the controlled use of ultrasonic waves?
items.answer: High-frequency ultrasonic waves possess immense practical utility due to their profound penetrative power and precise reflection capabilities. They are extensively used daily in non-invasive medical imaging, therapeutically shattering kidney stones, industrially detecting internal flaws within thick metal components, and powerfully operating maritime sonar systems to locate submerged underwater objects.

items.stem: A heavily equipped naval survey ship transmits a powerful vertical sonar pulse deep into seawater. The reflected signal successfully returns to the specialized onboard detector exactly 2.0 seconds later. If sound travels at exactly 1530 m/s in this seawater, how deep is the ocean floor?
items.answer: Sonar calculates depth by measuring round-trip travel time. The total time taken is 2.0 seconds, meaning the time strictly to reach the bottom is exactly 1.0 seconds. Using the standard formula d v t # = , =1530 *1.0 s =1530 meter The accurately calculated depth is precisely 1530 meters.

items.stem: While many animals share the human audible range, some possess distinctly different capabilities. Which of the following massive land animals is scientifically known to communicate across vast distances using extremely low- frequency infrasonic waves?
items.answer: While bats and dolphins famously utilize high-frequency ultrasonic waves for advanced echolocation, massive land mammals employ entirely different methods. Scientific studies confirm that elephants, alongside rhinoceroses and whales, successfully generate and detect extremely low-frequency infrasonic waves (below 20 Hz) to securely communicate with each other over immensely large physical distances.
